description: Proxmox live migration NUMA locality loss with 1G huge pages
system_prompt: You are a senior systems engineer with deep expertise in Linux internals, distributed systems, networking, and infrastructure operations. Think through the problem carefully — consider all interacting mechanisms before committing to an answer. Show your reasoning chain explicitly before stating conclusions.
user_message:
A Proxmox VE 8.x host (2-socket NUMA: socket 0 and socket 1, 256 GB RAM each)
runs a VM configured with:
  hugepages: 1G
  numa: 1       (NUMA topology exposed to the guest)
  vCPUs pinned to socket 0 cores
  memory pinned to socket 0 (memslot 0)

The VM runs an in-memory database (Redis-like workload, fully resident in RAM).
It is live-migrated to an identical target host. After migration, the workload
reports 3× higher P99 latency. numastat on the target shows:

  numa_miss: 47,832,441   (socket 1 satisfying socket 0 allocation requests)

(a) Describe the sequence of events during live migration that causes pages to
    land on the wrong NUMA socket. Be specific about QEMU's page fault behaviour
    on the target and how 1G huge page pre-allocation interacts with it.
(b) Explain why exposing NUMA topology to the guest (numa=1) makes the latency
    impact worse rather than better in this scenario.
(c) List the concrete steps — covering both host-side configuration before
    migration and post-migration remediation — to restore NUMA locality. Include
    the relevant Proxmox config knobs and sysfs paths.
